## Session handoff — census is STALE again; re-measure before doing anything

State at handoff: `in_progress`, zero merged commits.

**The recorded census is out of date, and by more than usual.** The correction comment above was
measured against a specific `origin/main`, and this session merged **45 changes** on top of that,
several of which added substantial code to `src/rebar` — including a ~300-line new module
(`_snapshot/delta_tree.py`) and additions to `cache.py`, `janitor.py`, `queue.py`,
`access_check.py`, `run_failure.py` and `gen_env_registry.py`.

So both the set of files near the 800-LOC cap and their headroom will have moved. Acting on the
recorded numbers would target the wrong files.

**What the next session should do FIRST:** re-run the census against current `origin/main` and
post the result, superseding the figure above, before selecting any extraction target. The
existing correction comment is itself a precedent for that — it exists because a prior census was
consumed after it went stale.

**Two constraints to carry in**, both re-confirmed in this session's work: the 800 cap is absolute
with no allowlist escape hatch, and splits must follow existing call-graph seams rather than being
mechanical — the module-size gate and the shrink-only complexity ratchet will both reject a split
that merely moves lines. An agent this session hit the ratchet by adding branches to a
near-ceiling function and had to extract along a seam instead.
